content_preview.summary: JAX 0.12.0, tagged October 19, adds erfcinv, a polynomial primitive, defremat and a proxy backend, and removes jax.custom_remat and support for AVX-only CPUs.

## Overview

JAX, the numerical computing and machine-learning library maintained in the jax-ml GitHub organization, published version 0.12.0. The [GitHub release page](https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/releases/tag/jax-v0.12.0) shows the tag was created on 2026-10-19, and the project's [changelog](https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) dates the release October 19, 2026. The release adds new numerical primitives, a way to customize rematerialization for custom gradients, and a backen...

editor_notes.content_quality: Briefing, 698 words (counted on body_markdown; range 300-800). Clear structure (Overview, What Is New, Proxy backend, Breaking Changes and Deprecations, Other Changes, What We Don't Know). Appropriate technical depth; neutral, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Two sources, both first-party (github.com/jax-ml). Read snapshots source-0.html.gz (CHANGELOG.md, 200, contains heading 'JAX 0.12.0 (October 19, 2026)', 'Haswell', 'Dropped support for NumPy 2.1', 'psend') and source-1.html.gz (release page 'Release JAX v0.12.0', published datetime 2026-10-19T11:18:24Z, marked Latest). Because the CHANGELOG snapshot is a large rendered GitHub HTML page, I additionally re-fetched the raw CHANGELOG.md from raw.githubusercontent.com and the release via the GitHub API (gh api repos/jax-ml/jax/releases/tags/jax-v0.12.0) and verified every bullet individually under the '## JAX 0.12.0 (October 19, 2026)' heading (not 0.11.x). Confirmed verbatim in substance: erfcinv; jax.lax.polynomial (faster, less memory for gradients); jax.custom_vjp.defremat (customizes rematerialization of a custom_vjp function under jax.remat; requires jax_custom_vjp3 and jax_remat3) - the title's 'Custom VJP Rematerialization' is accurate and not overstated; custom_gradient remat option; defremat_with_logs; at[].get strategy (gather/dynamic_slice/slice); generic_batching on defvjp; mxfp4 (E2M1 elements, E8M0 scale per block of 32; native on AMD gfx950, dequantize-and-dot fallback elsewhere); no_collectives; generalized eigh; ProfileSession/export_profile_data; experimental thunky (XLA:GPU ThunkExecutor); proxy backend (connects to an IFRT Proxy server such as Pathways on Cloud; JAX_PLATFORMS=proxy, JAX_BACKEND_TARGET e.g. grpc://localhost:29000). Breaking changes: jax.custom_remat removed with the exact migration recipe; x86-64 JAX and jaxlib require Intel Haswell or newer (roughly 2013, AVX2 and FMA; AVX-only CPUs unsupported; source builds still possible); NumPy 2.1 dropped, 2.2+ required; atleast_Nd return tuples; random.multinomial shape semantics; custom_vjp under vmap error; jnp.cross 2D removal (the 0.11.0 changelog deprecation says removal in 0.12.0 - consistent); jnp.array keyword-only args. Deprecations: only jax.lax.psend and precv are listed as deprecated, with no removal date stated; the article states no date, correctly. Other changes: web debugger localhost default, Bazel 9.2.0, accuracy items, hypot derivative at (0,0) NaN (previously +-0.5) - all confirmed. Both sources are first-party; no independent corroboration, appropriate for a release-notes Briefing. manifest suspicious_patterns null for both sources; no prompt-injection text observed.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All numbers, API names, version requirements and attributions trace to the changelog. One imprecision: the Overview says the release page 'shows the tag was created on 2026-10-19'. The release page shows only the release publication time (2026-10-19T11:18:24Z); the tag is lightweight (no tag date recorded) and points to the commit 'Prepare for JAX release 0.12.0' dated 2026-10-16T10:51:07Z (the GitHub release object was also created 2026-10-16 and published 2026-10-19). The changelog's own date of October 19, 2026 is correct. Filed as a clarification. The summary's 'tagged October 19' carries the same imprecision (release dated/published October 19).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; the 'What We Don't Know' section candidly notes the lack of adoption data and benchmarks.
editor_notes.originality: No prior JAX coverage in src/content/articles (grep for jax found only an unrelated PyTorch article). New topic.

recommendations: Say 'released' or 'published' on the date shown on the release page rather than 'tag was created'.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced first-party Briefing. Single minor date-wording clarification in a subordinate sentence; headline, summary substance and lead hold. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. The script's auto-verdict was APPROVE with no pattern-scanner hits.
